articles.title: 🤟 New Phone Can Transcribe Sign Language Into Text; Genuinely Useful Feature Accidentally Slips Into Product
articles.dateline: NEW YORK — reported in more than one language at once
paras: Google's new Pixel can reportedly transcribe sign language into text in real time — a genuinely wonderful accessibility feature that somehow snuck into a launch otherwise devoted to a glowing light and a slightly thinner bezel.

"We're proud of it," Google said, of a tool that actually helps people — a category of feature the industry occasionally rediscovers by accident. Advocates welcomed it warmly, while gently noting it should probably headline the keynote instead of playing third fiddle to the phone's new mood lighting.

articles.title: 💬 You Can Now Text An A.I. Unlimited Times; It Will Never, Ever Leave You On Read
paras: As of this month, you can send unlimited texts to a leading AI chatbot — finally granting humanity a correspondent who answers instantly, never tires of you, and has read every single message with alarming enthusiasm.

"It's always available," the company said, of a companion that will happily discuss your feelings, your grocery list, and the meaning of life at 3 AM without once suggesting you go to sleep. Relationship experts note it is either the cure for loneliness or an extremely patient enabler, and quite possibly both at once.

articles.title: 🩺 Your Phone Can Now Warn You About Diabetes; Also Deeply Concerned About That Third Cookie
articles.dateline: THE CLOUD CLINIC — reported between heartbeats
paras: Google says its new tools can act as an early-warning system for diabetes — a genuinely useful health advance that also, unavoidably, means your phone now holds opinions about your snacking and the emotional standing to share them.

"Early detection saves lives," experts noted, of technology that will help millions and simultaneously turn every device into a tiny, pocket-sized doctor who definitely saw what you just ate. Users welcomed the health benefits and braced for a future in which their phone sighs audibly at the vending machine.

articles.title: 📖 Samsung Unfolds The Galaxy Z Fold 8; Phone Now Opens Like A Book You'll Still Never Read
paras: Samsung officially unveiled the Galaxy Z Fold 8, its latest phone that folds open into a small tablet — continuing the noble quest to give you a bigger screen for the exact same three apps you already never close.

"It's thinner than ever," Samsung declared, of a device engineered to fold thousands of times and priced as though each fold were done by hand. Reviewers admit it is genuinely impressive, and that unfolding it in public still makes you feel, briefly, like a wizard consulting an ancient scroll.

articles.title: 🥊 Two Phone Assistants Enter A Turf War Over Your Dumbest Questions; Only One Can Set The Timer
articles.dateline: INSIDE THE DEVICE — reported from the front line
paras: Google's Pixel put its Gemini assistant at the center of an escalating AI-phone battle with Apple — meaning two of the world's most advanced artificial intelligences are now locked in mortal combat for the honor of answering "what's the weather."

"Our assistant is smarter," both companies insisted simultaneously, of rival systems capable of reasoning, planning, and still occasionally setting an alarm for the wrong 7 o'clock. Consumers, caught in the crossfire, report they simply want the one that will reliably text "running 5 min late" without first starting a philosophical discussion.

horoscopes.text: Your phone will express concern about your snack today. It means well. Eat the cookie anyway.
An A.I. will answer every text instantly tonight. Cherish it. It may be the only one who will.
Mercury folds like a Z Fold 8. Handle your week gently, and strictly along the existing crease.

tech_tip: If your phone offers unlimited A.I. texting, remember: 'available 24/7' is a feature for the app and a warning for you.
gadget_watch: The Pixel can now transcribe sign language and flag diabetes risk — genuinely good stuff — while Samsung's Z Fold 8 folds thinner than ever. Somewhere in the middle, two assistants are fighting to the death over your alarm clock.
